author: kirubaharan181
description: Classifies, checks and accepts or rejects evidence behind claims. Use when a gate needs proof. Do NOT use to produce the evidence itself.
purpose: Decides whether the evidence offered for a claim is good enough to pass a gate. It classifies the evidence, checks provenance and reliability, ties it to the claim and revision, assigns a confidence level, handles conflicting or missing evidence, and returns PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, INCONCLUSIVE, NEEDS_HUMAN_APPROVAL or WAIVED with reasons.
when_to_use: A gate, sign-off or approval depends on evidence.
A report claims work was done and the proof must be checked.
when_not_to_use: Producing the evidence: use the specialist skill.
Checking task completion overall: use definition-of-done.
Auditing controls across teams: use enterprise-governance.
prerequisites: The claim being gated and its gate id.
The evidence artifacts or immutable links.
No external API keys, paid services or network access are required; work uses files and tools already approved in the repository.
outputs: traceability from claim to evidence to revision
gate decision with status and limitations

decision_rules.situation: Evidence has no revision or timestamp
Evidence is for a different build
decision_rules.action: FAIL for this claim; request the correct evidence.
Prefer the one closer to the system and reproducible; record the conflict; do not average.

decision_rules.situation: Evidence is an example or illustration
decision_rules.action: Never count it; examples are marked example true.

decision_rules.situation: Only the producer vouches for the work
decision_rules.action: Request independent confirmation for high-risk gates.
BLOCKED; list exactly what is needed.

quality_gates: Each claim links to evidence with revision, method, executor and time
Confidence level is stated with reasons
Rejection reasons are specific and fixable

examples.title: Accept test evidence
examples.request: Gate: all unit tests pass for build 2.8.0.
examples.context: A CI log and report are attached.
examples.behavior: Check build id, command, executor, time and result in the log, then confirm that raw output matches the summary.
examples.output: PASS with confidence high; limitation: unit tests only.
examples.acceptance: Record lists artifact link, revision and limitations.

examples.title: Reject a claim
examples.context: Only a screenshot without date or revision.
examples.behavior: Mark INCONCLUSIVE because provenance is missing and request the scan output.
examples.output: INCONCLUSIVE with the exact missing items.

examples.title: Conflicting evidence
examples.request: Load test shows pass; monitoring shows errors at the same time.
examples.behavior: Compare timestamps and environment, record the conflict, and prefer production-measured data for production claims.
examples.output: Conflict record with decision rationale and escalation if unresolved.
examples.acceptance: Conflict is recorded, not averaged away.

limitations: Judges the evidence offered; it cannot discover evidence that does not exist.
Cannot prove authenticity beyond provenance fields it can check.
Gate decisions that need approval go to a named human.

troubleshooting.resolution: Request an immutable copy or hash.
Accept with a stated limitation or request a safer form.
Normalize scope and time, then compare.
